newsitem.title: USA: Lawmakers call for new moves to combat Medicare fraud.
newsitem.headline: Lawmakers call for new moves to combat Medicare fraud.

text.p: Members of Congress on Wednesday told the Clinton administration to beef up oversight of the Medicare program in light of a new audit showing up to $23 billion in incorrect payments last year alone.
"Taxpayers are being bilked to the tune of billions of dollars. Enough is enough. It is unconscionable, it is unacceptable. And it must stop," said Iowa Democratic Sen. Tom Harkin.

He asked the Department of Health and Human Services to develop a plan within 30 days to recover mispayments. Harkin also said the government should carry out additional audits and force the health industry, not taxpayers, to fund them.

Other senators called the overpayments unforgivable at a time when Congress was considering gradually raising the Medicare eligibility age to 67 from 65 and making other changes to help balance the budget and ensure the program's solvency.

The Department of Health and Human Services was due to make public on Thursday a national audit of more than 5,000 Medicare payments. The audit found numerous errors, though not all were necessarily fraud. Extrapolating from the sample the auditors estimated that there were between $17 billion and $23 billion in wrong payments last year.
That total represents up to 14 percent of total Medicare spending. Previous studies had estimated that about 10 percent of Medicare was lost to fraud and abuse.
An administration official said HHS would release a proposal on Thursday to clean up the system. The department already plans to expand anti-fraud efforts and has asked Congress for more authority.
According to a summary of the study released by the lawmakers, about one in three of the claims audited contained mispayments, with average payment errors of $670.
About 46 percent of Medicare payment claims were improperly documented. More than a third involved services that on later review were found not to be medically necessary.
